summary: Ernst Moritz Arndt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Greifswald (~1791–1793) and the University of Jena (~1793–1794). He held posts at Greifswald (~1800–1811) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1860).

Ernst Osiander was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren (~1843–1847) and the University of Tübingen (1847–1853, under Rudolf von Roth). He later served as Repetent at Maulbronn und Blaubeuren (~1852–1854) and Tübinger Stift (1857–1860).

Linguist Ernst Schwarz studied at the German University of Prague (~1914–1920) and the Deutsche wissenschaftliche Prüfungs-kommission für das Lehramt an Mittelschulen in Prag (~1920–1922). He held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1953 to 1963.

Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar Ernst Steinkellner earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~1957–1963) under Erich Frauwallner. He served as Director at Vienna (1973–2006) and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences' Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ernst Trumpp was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Tübinger Stift (~1846–1850) under Rudolf von Roth (~1847–1850), worked at East India House (~1854–1856), and became a professor at the University of Munich (~1874–1885).

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Ernst Waldschmidt studied at Kiel (~1916–1919) under Deussen and Sieg, and Berlin (~1920–1924) under Lüders, Francke, and Grünwedel. He worked at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1929) and held Göttingen's Indology chair (1936–1965).

Indologist and linguist Ernst Windisch studied at the University of Leipzig (1863–1868) under Curtius, Ritschl, Zarncke, and Brockhaus. He held chairs of comparative linguistics at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875) before returning to Leipzig as professor from 1877.

Ernst Zinn was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1947–1951), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (~1957–1978).

Sinologist Erwin Rousselle studied in Munich, Freiburg, Berlin, Darmstadt, and Heidelberg, under teachers including Krause, Walleser, and Staël-Holstein. He taught at Peking University (1924–1929), directed the Sino-Indian Institute (~1931–1938), and directed the China-Institut Frankfurt (1931, 1948).
Esben Andreasen, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, studied at the University of Copenhagen. He was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy Eshin Nishimura studied at Hanazono University, under Zenkei Shibayama, at Pendle Hill, and at Kyoto University (Ph.D.). He held positions at Hanazono University (1970, 2002–2005) and served as director of the Institute for Zen Studies.
Buddhist studies scholar Esho Kawasaki served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).
Esho Mikogami specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a professor at Ryukoku University until 2003 and served as president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

Esho Sasaki, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, served as an assistant professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

Esho Yamaguchi worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and later served as a professor at Osaka University (~1970–1982), holding an additional post at Ritsumeikan University.
Eshun Otsuka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and held a post there as a research student (attested 2013).

Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar Ester Bianchi earned a PhD from Ca' Foscari University of Venice and EPHE (~1999–2003) under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert. She held posts at Ca' Foscari (~2003–2006) and the University of Perugia (~2007).

Ethan Kroll, working in Indology and other fields, was associated with Baker McKenzie (attested 2012) and served as an editorial board member for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (attested 2012).
Philosopher Etienne Vermeersch studied at Ghent University (~1953–1965) and later served on the faculty at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.

Etsuaki Teraishi, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, served as an assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a special researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).
